coverage.rationale: Every spatial measurement depends on a stable body-diameter normalization from both recordings.
A collision-free 33-frame SSAG floor run with the opponent distant supplies the accepted sustained-movement observation.
coverage.limitation: The WCG comparison overlaps a shot and cannot exclude recoil, so it is retained but excluded; no second action-isolated run was found in the selected recordings.

coverage.rationale: A collision-free SSAG second-duel arc with no movement card supplies the accepted jump-height observation.
coverage.limitation: The WCG comparison contains a shot during the arc, so it is retained but excluded; no second isolated jump was found in the selected recordings.

coverage.rationale: The accepted SSAG arc supplies the visible rise time at the source's two-tick frame resolution.
coverage.limitation: The WCG comparison contains a shot during the arc, so it is retained but excluded; the accepted SSAG interval begins after takeoff and is a lower bound.

coverage.rationale: The SSAG opening loadout leaves projectile speed unchanged and supplies the accepted base-speed sample.
coverage.limitation: The independent WCG opening uses Thruster and Fast Forward, so its projectile sample is retained as a contaminated comparison and does not count toward coverage.

coverage.rationale: The SSAG opening provides a visible unmodified projectile-core radius.
coverage.limitation: At 640x360 the core is only about three pixels across, so a second recording would not materially improve the broad tolerance without higher-resolution media.

coverage.rationale: Pre-shot and post-shot body velocities from both opening rounds produce a low-confidence recoil impulse band.
Both opening loadouts leave block duration unchanged and expose the visible active shield.
Both recordings use a fixed 16:9 full-stage view with independently measured body scale.
One clean WCG ring-out exposes the boundary-to-result transition.
coverage.limitation: The selected SSAG opening death is projectile-driven rather than an observable ring-out, so no second out-of-bounds sample is claimed.

measurements.modifierControl: Neither visible starting card lists a shooter-recoil modifier, and the shooter is airborne and separated from players and platforms throughout the fitted horizontal interval.
measurements.method: Computed three-frame endpoint slopes immediately before and after the visible airborne muzzle event, then normalized their horizontal velocity difference by body diameter and ticks per frame.
measurements.notes: Concurrent player input remains an unresolved source of error, so the two-source recoil band is deliberately broad.
